name: Dunzo
one_liner: Hyperlocal app that would pick up and deliver anything in the city, later a 15-30 minute grocery dark-store service
story: Dunzo began as a WhatsApp concierge that would fetch anything, won Google's first direct investment in India (2017) and a $240M Reliance-led round in 2022 at roughly $775M. It pivoted into 15-minute dark-store grocery delivery just as Blinkit, Zepto and Swiggy Instamart out-spent it; salaries were delayed through 2023, buyout talks with Swiggy and BigBasket failed, and the app went dark in January 2025. Reliance wrote off its entire ~$200M stake (about Rs 1,645 crore) in FY25.

name: BluSmart
one_liner: All-electric ride-hailing service owning its fleet and charging superhubs
story: BluSmart ran an all-EV cab service in Delhi NCR and Bengaluru, with cars leased largely from its promoters' listed firm Gensol Engineering, and raised about $180M in equity and debt from bp ventures and others. In April 2025 SEBI found the Jaggi brothers had diverted loan money meant for EVs (Gensol bought only 4,704 of the 6,400 cars it borrowed Rs 978 crore for) into personal luxuries, barred them from markets, and BluSmart halted bookings almost overnight. Its asset-light app sat on top of a fleet it did not control, so the promoter fraud took the operator down with it.

name: GoMechanic
one_liner: Network of branded partner workshops for app-booked car servicing and repair
story: GoMechanic built a franchise network of car-service workshops and raised about $62M from Sequoia (Peak XV), Tiger Global, Orios and Chiratae, hitting a $285M valuation in 2021 and negotiating with SoftBank at up to $1B. In January 2023 the founders admitted inflating revenue; the SoftBank deal collapsed, 70% of staff were laid off and investors filed a police complaint. In March 2023 its assets went in an undisclosed slump sale to a Lifelong Group-led consortium (Servizzy), with founders left out.

name: Byju's
one_liner: K-12 and test-prep learning app with video lessons, sold on financed tablets by a large field sales force
story: Byju's became India's most valuable startup at $22B in 2022 after raising roughly $5.5B and spending billions on acquisitions (Aakash, WhiteHat Jr, Great Learning, Epic) during the pandemic edtech boom. As schools reopened demand fell, audits were delayed, it defaulted on a $1.2B US term loan and Prosus marked it to $5.1B in 2023; a 2024 rights issue was priced at about $220-250M. Lenders pushed its US unit into Chapter 11 and the parent into Indian insolvency in 2024, and the founder said it was 'worth zero'.

name: ZestMoney
one_liner: Buy-now-pay-later and checkout EMI platform for Indians without credit cards
story: Goldman Sachs- and Zip-backed ZestMoney offered BNPL and EMI credit at online checkouts and was valued at about $445-450M in 2021. A roughly $200-300M sale to PhonePe collapsed in 2023 over due diligence and bad-loan concerns, the founders resigned, and the company announced it would wind down in December 2023 after RBI tightened rules on fintech credit lines. DMI Group bought the remains in a January 2024 distress sale for an undisclosed sum.

name: Koo
one_liner: Multilingual Indian microblogging app positioned as a homegrown Twitter alternative
story: Koo surged in 2021 when Indian ministers adopted it during the government's spat with Twitter, raising $50-65M from Tiger Global, Accel, Kalaari and Blume and peaking at about $285M. Monthly actives fell from 9.4M in mid-2022 to about 3.1M by April 2023 as political interest faded and ads never paid for the servers. After buyout talks with Dailyhunt and others collapsed, it shut down in July 2024.

name: Hike
one_liner: Indian messaging app (Hike Messenger) that pivoted to the Rush real-money casual-gaming app
story: Kavin Bharti Mittal's Hike became a unicorn in 2016 ($175M Series D at $1.4B from Tencent, Foxconn, Tiger and SoftBank) as India's answer to WhatsApp, but WhatsApp won the market and Hike shut its messenger in January 2021. It pivoted to Rush, a real-money ludo and carrom app that drew 10M+ users and reportedly $500M+ gross revenue. India's 2025 ban on real-money online games cut its runway from seven months to four and Hike shut down entirely in September 2025.

name: Stoa School
one_liner: Online alternative-MBA program for working professionals
story: Stoa offered a cohort-based online alternative to the MBA for Indian professionals during the post-pandemic upskilling boom. It shut down in November 2024 without disclosing specific reasons, one of about a dozen funded Indian startups Inc42 counted as closing that year.
